learning_outcomes.text: The aim of the course is to acquire the ability to describe the state and movement of fluids, determine flow parameters in simple cases.

The student classifies fluids and determines their fundamental physical properties. Has structured knowledge of the methods used to describe the state and motion of fluids, including hydrostatics, kinematics, and dynamics of fluid flow.
The student is able to apply analytical and experimental methods to formulate and solve typical engineering problems related to fluid mechanics.
The student is able to plan and conduct experiments, perform fluid flow measurements, analyze obtained results and formulate engineering conclusions.
The student is able to work effectively as a member of an engineering team, demonstrating responsibility and communication skills in solving fluid mechanics problems.

syllabus_topics: Methods for describing the state and motion of fluids
Measurement of the critical Reynolds number
Determination of the friction loss coefficient
Measurement of average air velocity in an axisymmetric duct
Determination of the drag coefficient Cx for flow around a cylinder
Measurement of the boundary layer in a subsonic diffuser
Measurement of liquid viscosity using the Hagen–Poiseuille method

assessment_methods.method: active participation in laboratory classes and completion of all assigned measurements and reports

assessment_rules: The condition for passing the course is to achieve all required learning outcomes. This includes obtaining positive grades from laboratory reports and the final written or oral examination. Active participation in laboratory classes and completion of all assigned measurements and reports are mandatory. A minimum threshold of 50% of the total available points is required to pass the course. Additionally, students must demonstrate the ability to apply theoretical knowledge to solve practical problems related to fluid mechanics.
